prompt:
Return one bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. Each value must be a JSON string or null. Include all five keys; no Markdown, prose, or other output.

1. Isolate the single contact record in the user’s note. Read only its Label<sep>value lines, recognizing label variants and separators such as colon, equals, and tab. Do not use surrounding notes, signatures, email domains, or company suffixes as sources for other fields. Trim values and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent or empty values and these case-insensitive placeholders as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Missing fields are null except for the country fallback below.

2. Route values before formatting them. Reserve the country line for country. Among other record lines, a value containing @ is email; a value with at least seven digits and no characters other than digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . / after stripping a leading tel: and a trailing extension is phone. These content tests override labels. If the name-labeled value ends in a legal suffix and the company-labeled value does not, swap the name and company values. Match suffixes case-insensitively at the end, allowing an optional preceding comma: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

3. Resolve phone and country together. For any phone, discard leading tel: and a trailing extension of the form ext. 12, ext 12, x12, #12, or extension 12, where 12 stands for extension digits. Ignoring an opening parenthesis, a leading + or 00 makes it international. For international numbers, replace leading 00 with +, remove the optional (0), and remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses. Keep the written calling code.
Normalize the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish, or German country names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases in any case: UK or Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA or U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ. If the country is missing and the phone is international, fill country from the calling code only if it identifies one country. Shared codes, including +1 and +7, leave country null. This is the only exception to missing values staying null. If the country line disagrees with the international phone, keep both the line-derived country and the written phone calling code.
For a national phone, remove formatting punctuation and spaces, remove one leading trunk 0 if present, and prepend + and the calling code for the normalized country. Without a country, a national phone is null. Non-null phones are E.164: + followed by calling code and national significant number, with digits only after +.

4. Format the remaining fields. Name: split at the first comma to reorder Last, First to First Last, drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof (case-insensitive, optional dot), and uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Company: remove the trailing legal suffix and optional comma, trim, and uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word. Email: unwrap surrounding angle brackets and remove leading mailto: if present, accounting for either nesting order, then lowercase the whole address. Copy the address from the record; preserve its spelling and diacritics apart from the required casing. Keep Unicode letters and diacritics in all fields; never transliterate.
